title: Test your data pipeline basics
guideLabel: Re-read the parts of a pipeline

questions.q: Does a data pipeline have to reshape the data it moves?
options: Yes, every pipeline must clean and reformat its data
No, it may simply move data from one system to another
Only when it runs all day without stopping
Only when the data ends up in cheap file storage
questions.explain: IBM says a data pipeline may simply move data from one system to another. ETL is one kind of pipeline, so every ETL pipeline is a data pipeline but not the other way round.

questions.q: A pipeline loads data in groups at set times, say once a night. How fresh is the data in the report?
options: Updated the second something changes
Updated only when someone clicks refresh
Always a few seconds old
As old as the last run
questions.explain: That is a batch pipeline. It is simple, and it fits reports that can be a few hours or a day old. If you need seconds, that is when streaming earns its keep.

questions.q: A shop deletes a cancelled order from its database. The pipeline only looks for new or changed rows. What is the likely result?
options: The report shows the order twice
The pipeline stops working for good
The cancelled order stays in the report
The shop's website slows to a crawl
questions.explain: A row that is gone leaves nothing to find, so methods that only look for new or changed rows can miss real deletes. That gap is a big reason change data capture exists.

questions.q: Beside ingestion, transformation and storage, what else does a real pipeline need?
options: Scheduling, retries and alerts
A second warehouse as a backup
A dashboard for every table
A full copy of the source database
questions.explain: Something has to decide when each step runs, retry it when it fails and warn a person when it keeps failing. Without that, you have a script you are hoping keeps working.

questions.q: A step fails at 3 a.m. and the scheduler runs it again. What do you want to happen?
options: It adds the same rows again, to be safe
It skips the day and carries on
It gives the same result as if it had run once
It waits until someone approves the rerun
questions.explain: Retries are normal, duplicates are not. Airflow's docs say a retried task should produce the same outcome on every re-run, so build each step to be safe to run twice.
